Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has articles on:
вирус and компютърен вирус
Wikipedia bgWikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from Latin vīrus (“poison”), borrowed from some intermediate Western language (probably German Virus) or from Russian ви́рус (vírus).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈviros]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iros
  • Syllabification(key): ви‧рус

Noun

[edit]

ви́рус • (vírus) m

  1. (pathology) virus
  2. (computing) computer virus (a program which can covertly transmit itself between computers via networks (especially the Internet) or removable storage such as disks and USB drives, often causing damage to systems and data)

[edit]

Related terms

[edit]
  • вирусоло́гия (virusológija, “virology”)

[edit]

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
вирус
Wikipedia ru

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ви́русъ (vírus) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Virus, from Latin vīrus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈvʲirʊs]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

ви́рус • (vírus) m inan or m anim (genitive ви́руса, nominative plural ви́русы, genitive plural ви́русов, relational adjective ви́русный, pejorative collective вирусня́)

  1. (medicine) virus (DNA/RNA causing disease)
  2. (computing) computer virus

Usage notes

[edit]
  • With the exception of scientific or medical works, this noun is typically treated as inanimate.

Related terms

  • антиви́рус (antivírus), антиви́русный (antivírusnyj)
